stories.headline: Two American economists share the Nobel prize in economic sciences
stories.summary: Robert Hall and Michael Woodford have jointly won this year’s Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences. They were honoured for work on how the choices of households and firms underpin attempts to steady a whole economy. Hall is a professor at Stanford University and Woodford teaches at Columbia University.

stories.headline: Ülle Madise is sworn in as Estonia’s seventh president
stories.summary: Ülle Madise, a jurist who had been Estonia’s Chancellor of Justice since 2015, was sworn in as president on 12 October. The Riigikogu, the country’s parliament, had elected her on 2 September. She succeeds Alar Karis, who served one term and chose not to stand again.

stories.headline: Perseverance drives farther than any vehicle on another world
stories.summary: NASA’s Perseverance rover has now driven farther than any vehicle has on the surface of another world. It reached the mark after five and a half years on Mars, over ground that took the earlier Opportunity rover almost fifteen years to cover. Most of that distance was driven with the rover choosing its own course.

sources.excerpt: American economists Robert Ernest Hall and Michael Dean Woodford are jointly awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences for “microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation”.

Michael Dean Woodford (born 1955) is an American macroeconomist and monetary theorist who currently teaches at Columbia University. In 2026, he was awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences, along with Robert Hall.

Robert Ernest “Bob” Hall (born August 13, 1943) is an American economist who serves as a professor of economics at Stanford University, and as the Robert and Carole McNeil Senior Fellow at the Hoover Institution.

Ülle Madise (née Anton; born 11 December 1974) is an Estonian jurist who is the seventh president of Estonia, since 12 October 2026. She previously served as Chancellor of Justice from 2015 to 2026, having left the position upon assuming the presidency.

An indirect election took place in Estonia on 2 September 2026 to elect the president of Estonia, who is the country’s head of state. The Riigikogu elected Ülle Madise to serve in the office and she was sworn in as the 7th president on 12 October 2026.
The incumbent president, Alar Karis, had served one term and was eligible to seek a second consecutive term, but announced in June 2026 that he would not stand for re-election.
NASA’s Perseverance Mars rover has driven farther than any vehicle ever has on the surface of another world.
Perseverance reached the mark on the 2,006th Martian day, or sol, of its mission, covering in five and a half years a distance that took Opportunity almost 15.
Where NASA’s first Mars rover, Sojourner, assessed the path ahead using 20 measurement points, Perseverance processes 600,000 with every look.
